gaps.feature: skipWhenSignedIn tells an unreachable API apart from any other failure (onboarding.unreachable vs onboarding.failed toast)
gaps.detail: Confirmed. apps/web/src/lib/guards/skip-when-signed-in.ts line 30 picks the toast with `status === 0 || status >= 500`, where status comes from statusOf() in apps/web/src/lib/api-errors.ts lines 4-9. statusOf() returns 0 for any error that has no numeric `status` field. So a plain Error also gets the 'onboarding.unreachable' toast ('Couldn't reach Arrakit. Check your connection and reload.'), not 'onboarding.failed'. That plain Error can be a bug in the guard, a SyntaxError from `res.json()` in apps/web/src/lib/session.ts line 10, or a failure while the oRPC client decodes a response. saas-base, in apps/web/src/app/onboarding/onboarding.guards.ts isUnreachable(), counts only a real HttpErrorResponse with status 0 or >=500 as unreachable. Its spec 'opens the page on any other failure, logs it, and does not blame the connection' throws `new Error('bug')` from session() and expects the FAILED toast. docs/spec/auth-onboarding.md section 'Guard: skipWhenSignedIn' rule 4 (line 326) says the same thing. arrakit's apps/web/src/lib/guards/onboarding-guards.test.ts lines 124-143 cover only a network TypeError, a 503 and an RPC 403. There is no test for a plain Error, which is why this passes. Fix: count only a fetch TypeError (network failure) or status >= 500 as unreachable, and add a test where session() throws a plain Error and the guard shows the failed toast.

gaps.feature: Tenant-scoped lock() actually takes the requested row lock (FOR UPDATE / FOR SHARE)
gaps.detail: Confirmed, with low impact, and the file belongs to another owner. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/db/src/organization/tenant-db.ts:101-102 implements lock as `select().from(table).where(required(where)).for(strength)`. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/db/src/organization/tenant-db.test.ts:89-96 ('locks only its own rows') checks only which rows come back, and line 84 checks only that a missing where condition is refused. Nothing checks for a FOR UPDATE or FOR SHARE clause, so dropping `.for(strength)` keeps the tests green. A pattern to copy already exists: /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/db/src/organization/usage-locking.test.ts:18-33 logs the emitted SQL on PGlite with a drizzle logger, and its Postgres suite runs only when TEST_DATABASE_URL is set. The same approach could check the lock clause, and could also port the saas-base waiting test as a Postgres-only test. The members and invitations code does not call tenant-db lock() (a grep finds no `.lock(` outside tenant-db.test.ts). docs/ownership.md:20 assigns packages/db/src/organization/tenant-db.ts to platform, not organizations-members.
gaps.saasBaseRef: /home/luismdev/Projects/saas-base/libs/platform/data/src/tenancy/tenant-db.int.spec.ts:196 ('lock: a conflicting lock waits until the transaction holding the row ends')

gaps.feature: Billing settings and Plans show the API's own refusal text for 400/403 on getBilling, cancel/resume, portal and preview
gaps.detail: Confirmed with one correction. In saas-base these calls go through injectApiCall (this.call), which toasts `refusalMessage(error) ?? <screen text>` for a 400/403 that carries a message: Settings > Billing getBilling, setCancelled (cancel/resume) and openBillingPortal, and on Plans getBilling and previewPlanChange. Correction: the saas-base Plans getPlans load uses injectLoad -> toastOnError, which always shows the fixed text, so arrakit's `plans.loadFailed` (plans-page.tsx:66-68) already matches and is NOT part of the gap. In arrakit these handlers always toast the fixed i18n text: apps/web/src/components/settings/billing-section.tsx:73-77 (billing.get error effect, `notLoaded`), :87-90 (cancel onError, `notCancelled`), :95-98 (resume onError, `notKept`), :106-109 (portal() catch, `portalNotOpened`); apps/web/src/components/billing/plans-page.tsx:69-71 (billing.isError effect, `plans.billingLoadFailed`) and :76-79 (preview onError, `plans.priceFailed`). Only the plan switch (plans-page.tsx:89-92) uses paymentRefusal. The fix is `refusalMessage(err) ?? t(...)` from apps/web/src/lib/api-errors.ts (or the existing apiCall helper), which matches saas-base's 400/403 semantics. `billingRefusal` in apps/web/src/components/billing/api-refusal.ts (400/402/403/409) is unused outside its own test and is broader than saas-base. Tests only cover 502: billing-section.test.tsx:159,183,193 and plans-page.test.tsx:103,179. None checks that a 403 message (for example 'Change billing from the app.' or a demoted admin) reaches the toast for these calls.
gaps.saasBaseRef: apps/web/src/app/shared/api-call.ts:46-48 (refusalMessage), :66-77 (injectApiCall), :129-145 (toastOnError/injectLoad: no refusal pass-through); apps/web/src/app/signed-in/settings/billing-settings/billing-settings.ts:93 (getBilling), :118-131 (setCancelled), :133-141 (openPortal); apps/web/src/app/signed-in/plans/plans.page.ts:125 (getBilling), :132-145 (switchTo preview), :49-50 (getPlans via injectLoad, fixed text)

gaps.feature: The production web proxy sets x-forwarded-for from cf-connecting-ip when that header is present
gaps.detail: Confirmed. The only proxy is the Nitro route rules in /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/web/src/lib/api-proxy.ts:29-38. They use `{ xfwd: true, filterHeaders: ['x-forwarded-for'] }`, which drops the incoming XFF and forwards the TCP peer's address. No source in apps/web reads cf-connecting-ip; the string appears only in the docs. The web app has no server middleware directory. The spec /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/docs/spec/platform.md:908 requires the mapping for a production proxy. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/docs/gaps/iteration-2-fixes.md:79 records the omission as a deliberate choice: route rules are static, and the Cloudflare edge could set x-real-ip instead. It could still be fixed with an h3/Nitro server middleware. Behind Cloudflare without x-real-ip, sessions and the Better Auth rate limit key on the Cloudflare edge IP.

gaps.feature: The web proxy reads the API origin (API_ORIGIN) when it runs, not when it is built
gaps.detail: Confirmed. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/web/vite.config.ts:13 reads `process.env.API_ORIGIN` while the app builds and passes it into `nitro({ routeRules })`. The built /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/web/.output/server/index.mjs:615,629,643 hard-codes `http://localhost:3000/...` as the proxy targets. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/web/.env.example says API_ORIGIN is 'read at dev start / build time', so one build cannot be pointed at another API. saas-base's Pages Function reads env.API_ORIGIN on every request. It could be fixed with a runtime proxy handler or middleware that reads process.env.

gaps.feature: apps/api/.env.example carries the saas-base operator guidance
gaps.detail: Confirmed. The spec /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/docs/spec/platform.md:948 says to port the saas-base comments. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/api/.env.example leaves out six notes, though the code enforces or depends on most of them. (1) The MCP endpoint <BETTER_AUTH_URL>/api/mcp and its discovery URL /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp. (2) The Google and Microsoft redirect URIs <BETTER_AUTH_URL>/api/auth/callback/{google,microsoft}. (3) The Entra app must emit the optional `email` and `xms_edov` claims; packages/auth/src/social.ts enforces this. (4) BETTER_AUTH_SECRET needs at least 32 random characters. The example ships the placeholder `change-me-to-a-long-random-string`. (5) Production refuses to start without Google (packages/auth/src/config.ts:38), DATABASE_URL and R2_* (packages/db/src/config.ts:40-44), or RESEND_API_KEY. The file says only 'the buttons hide when unset'. (6) Checkout answers 503 without all three STRIPE_* keys. This is documentation only and low impact.
